transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-11
Start: 15:00 UTC (08:00 PDT)
Duration: 50 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Clarke (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (CSM) / Lina Gomez (Stratos Platform Lead), Rajiv Menon (SRE), Claire Dupont (Security), Omar Aziz (PM)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
- Quick results review from pilot week 3: latency stable but a couple of degradation spikes on route /invoices-match under burst.
- Agreed to tighten canary gating thresholds and run a dry-run with 5% traffic before 20% ramp.
- Action: Redwood to update runbook, SRE to share prod profiles, security to confirm key management window.

Topics: cutover sequencing, canary thresholds, telemetry/alerting, rollback criteria, smoke tests, security gating (KMS/SOC2)

Questions (auto):
- What exact telemetry signals will gate the 5% -> 20% ramp?
- Do we need a dedicated fallback model pinned to CPU-only nodes for degradation events?

----- Transcript -----
[00:00] Maya Patel: All right uh good morning everyone thanks for joining, um we'll go for about 50 minutes today, quick agenda, results recap, tuning items, cutover runbook updates and then dry-run scheduling.
[00:18] Lina Gomez: Morning, yep that's the right agenda. We had a hectic week, saw two spikes on our end when external webhook burst hit which, uh caused the KV cache miss to spike i think?
[00:30] Ethan Clarke: Right, we see that in telemetry too, the KV cache hit-rate dropped briefly and the runtime had to re-warm some kv pages. The latency bump aligned with those cache misses so it's likely prefix-cache invalidation from the webhook fanout.
[00:48] Rajiv Menon: Clarify, uh the spike was at 03:14 UTC last Friday, right? It was about a 4x throughput blip for ~90 seconds.
[01:00] Lina Gomez: yes that's the one.
[01:04] Ethan Clarke: And to add, the model variant fallback kicked in for some requests — not a full degrade but we routed to a quantized 8-bit fallback for a small subset which increased tokenization time.
[01:20] Omar Aziz: Sorry, quick question, when you say fallback which path is that? Is that the cpu-only fallback we discussed or a smaller parameter model?
[01:30] Ethan Clarke: Good question — it's a lower-capacity GPU-backed variant with a different kernel profile; we have CPU fallbacks as well but those are reserved for full-region outages, we didn't trigger that. There may be some naming mismatches in the logs, we've seen labels like "fallback-x" sometimes show up as "fallback-1a" in customer logs.
[01:52] Claire Dupont: That's slightly worrying for security/audit — if labels differ we need mapping for our SRE playbooks.
[02:00] Maya Patel: Absolutely we'll add a mapping table in the runbook v2.

[02:10] Ethan Clarke: Quick results bullets from the week: overall p50 ~ 85ms, p95 ~ 420ms on the heavy L2 routes, error rate stayed under 0.3% except the webhook window where it spiked to 1.8% briefly. Cost numbers looked within expected band.
[02:32] Lina Gomez: The issue is the client-observed tail on /invoices-match — we have important SLA commitments there.
[02:38] Rajiv Menon: For cutover gating we recommend putting stricter p95 thresholds for those top-10 routes, and require zero increase in error-rate for the 5% canary window.
[02:50] Maya Patel: Ok so let's be explicit. Proposed canary plan: start with 1% smoke flow for 15 minutes (synthetic smoke, warm KV), then 5% for 30 minutes with telemetry gates: p95 increase <= 10% absolute (not relative?), error-rate delta <= 0.2% absolute, throughput stable within 10%. If gates pass, we ramp to 20% over 30 minutes, then 50% and finally cutover.
[03:18] Claire Dupont: Is the p95 absolute delta measured against baseline period or rolling baseline? For audit we need a defined baseline window.
[03:26] Ethan Clarke: We'll measure against the 30-minute baseline prior to canary start and include rolling comparison in telemetry. We'll publish the baseline snapshot in the runbook.
[03:36] Lina Gomez: For our SRE on-call, we need explicit abort conditions. Like if p95 > 600ms or error-rate > 1% for 10 minutes we abort.
[03:46] Rajiv Menon: Add also if KV cache miss ratio > 15% for 5 minutes, abort — that was a signature of the webhook event.

[04:00] Omar Aziz: Regarding A/B experiments mentioned in docs, can we run a 10% A/B test for new ranking prompt to validate quality before full cutover? That would be helpful for product.
[04:12] Ethan Clarke: Yes we can do parallel A/B with traffic steering. The main difference is we treat A/B as quality gating not infra gating; so traffic split won't affect capacity but we'll still monitor latency gates for safety.
[04:26] Maya Patel: Note: A/B experiment requires separate metric sets for quality evals; Redwood can ingest their eval harness results if Stratos shares the prompt sets.

[04:40] Lina Gomez: We'll share the top 200 prompts and the scoring harness.
[04:44] Claire Dupont: Security question: For the canary we need to confirm KMS rotation doesn't happen during the 48-hour safety window. We also want to lock down audit logs for that period.
[04:56] Maya Patel: Understood — we'll mark the 48-hour window as audit-locked in our calendar and provide the runbook step to verify key status prior to canary start.

[05:08] Ethan Clarke: On telemetry, recommended alert set: p95 increase >10% (warning), p95 > 600ms (critical), error-rate > 0.5% (warning), error-rate > 1% (critical), KV miss ratio > 12% (warning), KV miss > 15% (critical), dropped tokens > 0.5% (critical). We'll attach suggested Grafana dashboards and sample queries.
[05:34] Rajiv Menon: Can you also publish the tracing span that correlates cold kv re-warm with token generation time? That will help our root cause analysis.
[05:42] Ethan Clarke: Yes, we can export that trace snippet and add a troubleshooting section.

[06:00] Jordan Lee: Quick ops note — the runbook will include an explicit rollback command set (api calls and traffic policy flip) and a postmortem template to capture the event.
[06:12] Lina Gomez: We also want simulated chaos run during dry-run — small network jitter and a darker fallback exercise to ensure rollback steps are smooth.
[06:20] Maya Patel: Good call. For the dry-run we'll schedule a controlled chaos window limited to the staging path and one witness engineer.

[06:34] Omar Aziz: Timing question — what's the preferred maintenance window? Our business peak is 13:00-17:00 UTC so we'd prefer outside that.
[06:44] Maya Patel: We recommend early morning UTC to reduce user impact; proposed window 05:00 - 08:00 UTC. But we can align to Stratos preference.

[07:00] Claire Dupont: A compliance ask — will Redwood preserve immutable logs for 90 days post-cutover for audit?
[07:08] Maya Patel: Yes; retention can be configured, we'll confirm in the SOC2 package and include a retention config snippet in the runbook.

[07:22] Ethan Clarke: On smoke tests: Ethan -> (laugh) that's me, I'll own building smoke scripts. We'll include three tiers: synthetic latency, correctness (top-20 prompt validation), and end-to-end checkout flow.
[07:36] Rajiv Menon: For the e2e flows we need to stub third-party webhooks to avoid external fanout. Can Redwood provide a mock endpoint?
[07:44] Ethan Clarke: Yes we can supply a lightweight webhook stub in the test harness.

[08:00] Lina Gomez: Can we talk about logs correlation? Our observability uses an internal trace id. The Redwood token IDs don't map natively.
[08:10] Maya Patel: We'll add a tracing mapping: Redwood request_id -> Stratos trace_id propagation header example, and a helper script to join logs.

[08:26] Omar Aziz: Any concerns on capacity — we talked about reserved pools earlier, are we still on dedicated capacity plan?
[08:34] Maya Patel: You're on the Dedicated trial with a small reserved GPU pool plus burst to shared capacity. For cutover we recommend bumping reserved to cover 1.5x expected 95th percentile for 24 hours then release. We'll propose a temporary bump in the runbook so billing ops can sign off.

[08:54] Claire Dupont: If billing is a blocker we need an automated throttle policy that slows non-critical requests during canary.
[09:02] Ethan Clarke: We can implement route-based QoS and deprioritize internal analytics calls during canary.

[09:12] Lina Gomez: ok, concrete sequence in runbook we want: preflight checks (KMS, baseline snapshot, run smoke), start 1% synthetic, 5% user canary with gates, 20% ramp, monitor 2 hours, 50% ramp, final cutover. Each step has abort criteria.
[09:30] Maya Patel: We'll publish runbook v2 with that flow and an abbreviated checklist for on-call. We'll also attach the rollback command set and the Grafana dashboard links. Link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/stratos-cutover-v2 (note: placeholder).

[09:50] Jordan Lee: Proposed dry-run on 2026-09-16 10:00 PDT, duration 90 minutes — include chaos window and A/B quality check.
[10:00] Claire Dupont: That works for security to observe.

[10:12] Maya Patel: Final quick recap of action items...
[10:18] Lina Gomez: Also add: can we get a one-page "what to watch" that lists top 6 dashboards and who acknowledges alerts?
[10:26] Maya Patel: Yes, short ops cheat sheet will be included.

[10:34] Ethan Clarke: I'll share smoke test repo and a sample payload set.
[10:38] Rajiv Menon: We'll send prod traffic profile CSV and top 20 routes.

[10:46] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone; we'll follow up with the runbook and schedule the dry-run.

[10:54] (meeting ends)

----- End of transcript -----

References mentioned: runbook link (placeholder) https://redwood.internal/runbooks/stratos-cutover-v2, smoke-test repo: https://github.com/redwood-internal/stratos-smoke, shared prompts drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/sample-prompts (note: access as needed).

Notes about transcript quality: auto-transcription mislabels some fallback names and occasional punctuation issues; speaker overlaps around 04:00-05:00 cause short crosstalk lines.
